rationale.a: Retrofit the system immediately with R-410A refrigerant; R-22 leaks are critical emergency warranting urgent replacement.
rationale.b: Switch to R-32 refrigerant by adding 2 kg to boost pressure; R-32 is compatible with R-22 systems if properly charged.
rationale.d: Continue operating with R-22 indefinitely; the 2040 deadline allows servicing existing systems until that date with any available refrigerant.
rationale.correct: R-22 is banned from manufacture and import since 2015 in developed countries; Philippines phase-out deadline is 2040 per RA 8749 (Ozone Layer Protection Act). For existing R-22 systems, servicing with recovered/recycled refrigerant is permitted as a temporary measure until system replacement. Do NOT retrofit with R-32 or R-410A without manufacturer approval and system redesign (oil type incompatibility, charge amounts differ). Recommended action: Repair the leak with recovered R-22 (if available through licensed recovery contractor), or schedule system replacement with R-32 split unit (~₱40,000–50,000 per TR). New systems must NOT use R-22. Source: LEA-UTIL-002-04 Refrigerant Standards section; RA 8749 Ozone Layer Protection Act.
rationale.takeaway: R-22 servicing for existing systems uses recovered/recycled refrigerant only; retrofitting with newer refrigerants requires manufacturer approval and system redesign. Plan replacement with R-32 (recommended standard) within 5–10 years before R-22 supply dries up.
